parsed_output.analysis: The specification describes a single composite state PumpControl that contains three substates PumpState, WaterState and MethaneState. The system starts in PumpControl and then first enters PumpState, with the ability to move to WaterState and MethaneState from PumpControl based on conditions. The PlantUML model re-defines PumpControl three times, treats the substates as top-level targets of external transitions from PumpControl, and gives each re-definition its own initial [*] entry, so the containment and initial-entry semantics are broken.

issues.issue: PumpControl composite is defined three times with only one substate each instead of one composite containing all three substates
issues.reason: The specification states PumpControl contains three main substates PumpState, WaterState and MethaneState together. The model creates three separate definitions of PumpControl, each isolating a single substate, so there is no single composite with all three substates.
issues.where: state PumpControl { [*] --> PumpState ... }, state PumpControl { [*] --> WaterState ... }, state PumpControl { [*] --> MethaneState ... }

issues.issue: Substates are modelled as external targets of PumpControl instead of nested substates
issues.reason: With substates, entry to a substate is an internal transition of the composite, not an external transition from PumpControl to a peer state. The model treats PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState as top-level states reachable from PumpControl.
issues.where: PumpControl -down-> PumpState : Activate Pump; PumpControl -down-> WaterState : Monitor Water Flow; PumpControl -down-> MethaneState : Monitor Methane Flow

issues.issue: Initial entry into PumpControl is ambiguous and contradicts the required first substate
issues.reason: The specification says the system first transitions to PumpState substate. The model defines an initial [*] --> PumpState in one definition and also initial [*] --> WaterState and [*] --> MethaneState in the other two re-definitions, implying the composite could start in any of the three substates.
issues.where: state PumpControl { [*] --> PumpState } and state PumpControl { [*] --> WaterState } and state PumpControl { [*] --> MethaneState }

issues.issue: Un-specified exit transitions from substates to the composite final
issues.reason: The specification describes only entry to the three substates from PumpControl based on conditions and does not define deactivation / stabilization exits back to/from PumpControl. The model adds exit transitions to [*] inside the composite that are not described in the specification.
issues.where: PumpState --> [*] : Pump Deactivated; WaterState --> [*] : Water Flow Stabilized; MethaneState --> [*] : Methane Flow Stabilized

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
